articles.title: How AI decision models could change content moderation
articles.summary: On Tuesday, Musubi announced a lightweight decision model made for real-time moderation called PolicyLM-1.7B, released with open weights.
articles.paragraph: On Tuesday, Musubi announced a lightweight decision model made for real-time moderation called PolicyLM-1.7B, released with open weights. AI How AI decision models could change content moderation Russell Brandom 1:35 PM PDT · October 6, 2026 As decision models spread across the industry, a company called Musubi has a new idea for how to put them to work: moderating content. On Tuesday, Musubi announced a lightweight decision model made for real-time moderation called PolicyLM-1.7B, released with open weights. The idea is to take a content policy written in plain English and apply it to messages in under 50 milliseconds.

articles.title: AI computing startup Lambda to raise $4B ahead of planned IPO
articles.summary: Nvidia-backed Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation ahead of a planned 2027 IPO, led by Coatue and Blackstone.
articles.paragraph: Nvidia-backed Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation ahead of a planned 2027 IPO, led by Coatue and Blackstone. Cloud provider Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation, marking what could be its last private round before a planned 2027 IPO, according to The Wall Street Journal. Coatue Management and Blackstone are leading the round. A letter to investors reviewed by the Journal shows Lambda’s backlog grew from $15 billion in June to $50 billion in September. While that might look like a hearty increase in demand, much of that increase appears to be driven by a $35 billion commitment from one company: Anthropic, which signed a deal with Lambda in late August.

articles.title: The next hurdle for AI agents: getting websites to let them in
articles.summary: Personal AI agents promise to shop, book flights, and make reservations for you. But deliberate blocks and anti-bot defenses are getting in the way, leaving consumers caught in the middle.
articles.paragraph: Personal AI agents promise to shop, book flights, and make reservations for you. But deliberate blocks and anti-bot defenses are getting in the way, leaving consumers caught in the middle. A new standard aims to help. AI The next hurdle for AI agents: getting websites to let them in Sarah Perez 12:56 PM PDT · October 6, 2026 Personal AI agents, like Meta’s Muse, Instinct, ChatGPT’s Dots, and others, are kicking off a new wave of consumer AI that involves more than just responding to queries. These AI agents can actually get things done on users’ behalf, like booking flights, making dinner reservations, ordering groceries, and more, all without having to be technical enough to set up OpenClaw or some other agent on your own computer.

articles.title: "US could be writing its own losing ticket": Amazon warns against 100+ AI data center bans as it pledges $1 billion to defuse AI backlash
articles.summary: Facing over 100 proposed moratoriums, Amazon offers $1 billion to host communities and expands Maryland nuclear power.
articles.paragraph: Amazon says banning AI data centers could cost America its lead, then dangles $1 billion at the towns hosting them More than 100 proposed moratoriums on new facilities are under consideration across the country, creating another obstacle for companies expanding computing capacity. Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman argued that restricting data center construction would hurt the country's competitiveness in AI. Residents and lawmakers increasingly question electricity demand, water consumption, environmental effects and the benefits delivered by large computing facilities. “If these measures are enacted, the U.S. could be writing its own losing ticket to this race, and the consequences would last generations,” said Matt Garman, Amazon Web Services (AWS) CEO.

articles.title: Massive 1.5 million sq ft data center campus planned for West Texas — bringing the state's total regional AI investment to $12 billion
articles.summary: Crusoe plans two $4.8 billion Jayton data centers, expanding its West Texas infrastructure alongside major projects in Childress and Abilene.
articles.paragraph: Crusoe just filed for two giant Texas data centers worth $4.8B, and almost nobody knows who will move in Each facility will cover 759,260 sq ft, creating nearly 1.52 million sq ft of new computing space across the proposed site. Applications filed with Texas regulators place the buildings along Country Road 233 and P2390 in Kent County, without providing specific street addresses. Construction at the Jayton site is scheduled to start in January 2027, with the first facility expected online in May 2029 and the second in July. The filings classify both structures as "spur buildings" connected to Project Hyper, a separate Crusoe development currently being built in Childress.

articles.title: 'If we do something, it has to be authentic to that community — it has to meet a certain bar of performance and what we have right now isn’t quite there’: Bose president Raza Haider’s message to gamers on a new headset is to ‘absolutely stay tuned'
articles.summary: Bose president Raza Haider has told gamers asking for a new version of its QC35 II headset to "absolutely stay tuned."
articles.paragraph: Bose president Raza Haider has told gamers asking for a new version of its QC35 II headset to Speaking in an exclusive interview with TechRadar, Haider acknowledged that there haven't been too many Bose gaming audio products in recent years, aside from the 2021 QC35 II gaming headset, and that the audio manufacturer is aware that the gaming community is filled with "very passionate users" who hope for more hardware from Bose. Haider explained that although the company produced the headset in the past, it didn't, "I don't think [it] resonated because it wasn't truly authentic," and satisfying the gaming community would be a top priority for a new iteration.

articles.paragraph: Allen Schnibben's interest in space started when he was a child. "I picked up some books about the solar system when I was in elementary school. In middle school, I got a telescope and I started observing the night sky as a hobby," said Schnibben, a computer scientist at Sandia National Laboratories. "My entire life, I've had an interest in space." Now, Schnibben collects data on satellites at Sandia's SOHBRIT facility, a 12-foot-wide (3.7-meter-wide) observatory.

articles.title: Google Launches Nano Banana 2.1: Better Than Its Predecessor at Half the Price
articles.summary: Google's new image model, Nano Banana 2.1, is live. It costs about half as much as its predecessor, but the performance claims come from Google's own tests.
articles.paragraph: Google's new image model, Nano Banana 2.1, is live in Gemini, Search, and Google Ads. It costs about half as much as its predecessor. Google on Tuesday released Nano Banana 2.1, the newest version of the AI model that turns a typed sentence into a picture, or edits a photo you already have. It's rolling out in the Gemini app, Google Search's AI Mode, Google Ads and developer tools including Google AI Studio, Flow and Stitch. The original Nano Banana made Gemini a hit. In September 2025, its trick of turning selfies into collectible figurines pushed Gemini to No. 1 on both major app stores, dethroning ChatGPT after nearly three years. Alphabet's market value topped $3 trillion in the same stretch. Version 2 arrived in February, built on Gemini 3.1 Flash Image.

articles.title: Circle Welcomes DJ Khaled to 'Team USDC' and Crypto Twitter Is Furious
articles.summary: Nothing in Circle's posts announces a sponsorship, but replies dug up Khaled's 2018 SEC settlement over a crypto fraud he promoted. The internet never forgets.
articles.paragraph: Nothing in Circle's posts announces a sponsorship, but replies dug up DJ Khaled's 2018 SEC settlement over a crypto fraud he promoted. Circle, the issuer behind the USDC stablecoin, welcomed rapper DJ Khaled to “team USDC” in a post on X on Monday—and Crypto Twitter lost its collective mind. But it’s probably not what it seems. Here’s what happened, and what appears to have caused the drama: USDC's official X account posted a photo of DJ Khaled wearing a Chelsea jersey with "USDC by Circle" across the chest, captioned "Another one," a nod to his signature catchphrase. About four hours later, Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire shared it with a note addressed to the rapper: "DJ Khaled welcome to team USDC." Nothing in either post announces a sponsorship, an ambassador role, or any money.

articles.title: Someone Scraped 5.6 Billion TikTok Videos and Put the Data on Hugging Face for Free
articles.summary: A developer posted metadata for about 5.6 billion public TikTok videos, scraped through the app's private API in a way TikTok's terms prohibit. The free dataset also doubles as a storefront.
articles.paragraph: A developer posted metadata for about 5.6 billion public TikTok videos, scraped through the app's private API in a way TikTok terms prohibit. A developer who goes by hashfunction has posted metadata for about 5.6 billion public TikTok videos on the open-source AI repository Hugging Face, free to download. The dataset, published under the datasocial account, runs from July 2014 through October 2026. It's metadata, not footage. Each row carries the caption, hashtags, sound ID, on-screen text, TikTok Shop product and seller IDs, and counts for views, likes, comments, shares, saves, and downloads. The whole thing is 460 GB of Parquet files, one per month. Some fields are TikTok's own labels: whether a video is flagged as AI-generated, and whether TikTok keeps it off the For You page.
